keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Schaumburg row). The page gives no area and no boundary; it names Rinteln (capital, founded by Adolf IV with Stadthagen) and Schauenburg Castle 'near Rinteln on the Weser', and does not name Bückeburg. A 15 km circle (about 707 km2) centred between Rinteln, Bückeburg and Stadthagen (9.15E 52.27N) is a soft stand-in. The Holstein and Stormarn rule of the Schauenburg counts, and Holstein-Pinneberg 'until 1640', are not drawn: they belong with Holstein. Revised after review: the first shape was a 22 km circle at Rinteln (about 1,520 km2), 2.3 to 2.6 times the area of the present Landkreis Schaumburg (the reviewer's 676 km2). The County page says only that the territory 'was more or less congruent with the present district Landkreis Schaumburg' and the district page that it 'essentially duplicates the borders of Schaumburg at the time of the Middle Ages'; neither page gives an area (the district page's area fields are blank), so 676 km2 is the reviewer's figure, not a page's. The start is now 1106 (the Adolf I page: 'first Count of Schauenburg from 1106'; the County page: 'probably ... in 1106'); the infobox 1110 is the Holstein appointment. landgraviate-of-hesse-kassel still draws the 22 km Rinteln circle for its Schaumburg gain; that dossier was not touched in this repair.

ledger.note: 1640: the house dies out and the county is split. 'After the childless death in 1640 of Count Otto V, the House of Schaumburg became extinct.' 'The County of Schaumburg proper was partitioned among the agnatic Schaumburg heirs into three parts': the eastern portion went to Hesse-Cassel in personal union, 'the largest portion became the County of Schaumburg-Lippe', a third to the Principality of Lüneburg (infobox end 1640: 'partitioned to create Schaumburg-Lippe, with the remainder going to Hesse-Kassel'). The page locates none of the shares. Revised after review: the three shares are now drawn as separate events (Hesse-Cassel's eastern portion and Lüneburg's part are the two losses just before; this dissolve carries the remainder). The cells are readings (the gazetteer grid is about 16 km, so each share is one cell). The Hesse-Kassel dossier dates its gain of 'most of the County of Schaumburg' 1648 (Peace of Westphalia) and calls it the largest part; this page dates the partition 1640 and makes Schaumburg-Lippe the largest: the pages disagree and 1640 is used here.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Schaumburg row.

SCOPE. Infobox 1110 to 1640. The page is thin: it dates only 1106 (first Lord of Schauenburg, 'probably'), 1110 (appointment to Holstein and Stormarn), 1559 (Reformation) and 1640 (Otto V dies, partition). Holstein and Stormarn, and Holstein-Pinneberg 'until 1640', are Holstein topics; only the Weser county is drawn. The founding event is therefore confidence 1 for the land.

SHAPE. Rinteln 9.08E 52.19N 22 km, as in landgraviate-of-hesse-kassel's 1648 Schaumburg gain. No area on the page. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Rinteln', 'Stadthagen', 'Schaumburg'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The 1640 shares: the page says three parts (Hesse-Cassel's eastern portion, the largest portion as Schaumburg-Lippe, a part of the Principality of Lüneburg) and does not locate them; the Kassel dossier of this batch has a 1648 gain of 'most of the County of Schaumburg' from a different page, which conflicts with Schaumburg-Lippe holding the largest portion. The Westphalia terms (1648) are not on this page. (2) The page gives no date for Stadthagen, Rinteln or the castle. (3) The Münster share some sources mention is not on the page.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: county-of-schaumburg-lippe (1640-1806 and later; suggested slug), none beyond that (stem-duchy-of-saxony exists).

REVISION 2026-10-25 (after review). (1) Shape: 22 km Rinteln circle replaced by a 15 km circle at 9.15E 52.27N (about 707 km2) in the keyframe, found, dissolve and predecessor/successor lands; the reviewer's 676 km2 (present Landkreis Schaumburg) is not on any page opened (County page: 'more or less congruent with the present district'; the district page's area fields are blank). (2) Start: 1106 instead of 1110 (Adolf I page: 'first Count of Schauenburg from 1106'; County page: 'probably ... in 1106'); the 1110 of the infobox is the Holstein appointment, which the Adolf I page dates 1111; confidence 2. The page 'Adolf I, Count of Schauenburg and Holstein' does not exist under that title (url_not_found); 'Adolf I, Count of Holstein' loaded. (3) The three-way partition of 1640 is drawn as two losses (Hesse-Cassel's eastern portion, Lüneburg's part) and a dissolve to Schaumburg-Lippe for the remainder; the cells are readings, the gazetteer grid is about 16 km. DISAGREEMENT between pages: the Hesse-Kassel dossier dates 'most of the County of Schaumburg' to Hesse-Kassel in 1648 (Peace of Westphalia) and this page makes Schaumburg-Lippe the largest portion in 1640; the Kassel dossier (verdict fix, not touched in this repair) should say so, take the 15 km circle and date the Hessian share 1640.
